name: walls_at_sixty_degrees_do_not_print
why: The other half of the criterion of the entry: «on a part with a known face at 60 degrees the operation classifies it as unsupported». The four walls are made with `draft`, which tilts them by an angle one chooses -- so the face at 60 degrees is not drawn by hand and hoped for: it is built by an operation that in turn measures what it did.
_why_flip_is_needed: THIS LINE COST A RED, and it is the reasoning that comes instinctively and is wrong. Without flipping, the draft widens the part going downwards: it becomes a frustum of a pyramid resting on the wide base, which is the shape that holds itself up -- the walls overhang OUTWARDS and their normals look UP. The bench answered «0 overhanging faces» and it was the bench that was right. The shape that overhangs is the one that NARROWS going down, that is the upside-down frustum: that is obtained with «flip», and indeed the part loses volume instead of gaining it. The volume, here, is the sign of what is being built.
_why_three_thresholds: At 45 degrees it does not print, at 70 it does. If the threshold were not used -- if it were written inside -- the two answers would be the same, and nobody would notice looking only at the case at 45.

expect.why: THE SIGN SAYS THE SHAPE. It drops because it narrows towards the bottom: it is the upside-down frustum of a pyramid, that is the shape that overhangs. If here it grew, we would have built the one that holds itself up and the next step would prove nothing.

expect.tolerance_why: the angle is derived from the normals of the triangles, which are single-precision floating point
expect.why: THE NUMBER THAT CLOSES THE CIRCLE. The draft tilted the walls by 60 degrees from the vertical, and the check -- which knows nothing of the draft and looks only at the geometry -- finds 60 again. Two independent roads to the same number.
THE THRESHOLD IS REALLY USED. Same part, same geometry: changing only the number the answer flips. If the threshold were written inside, this step would give 4 like the one above.

AND TURNED AROUND THE PART PRINTS. Printed the other way round, the upside-down frustum is back resting on the wide base: the same geometry, the same threshold, and no overhang. It is the answer to the question «what if I printed it turned over?» without turning the part.
